questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend checking access in a specific layered order rather than jumping to the most recently changed setting?
options: Because Salesforce evaluates access in that order, and following it avoids checking the wrong layer first
Because the order doesn't actually matter, it's just a convention
Because object permissions are always the cause of every problem
Because field-level security must always be checked last
questions.explain: The layered order (object permissions, FLS, OWD, hierarchy, sharing, restriction rules) mirrors how Salesforce actually evaluates access, which is why troubleshooting should follow it.

questions.q: A user can see a record but not one specific field on it. Which layer does that point to first?
options: Org-wide defaults
Role hierarchy
Field-level security
Restriction rules
questions.explain: Record-level access and field-level security are independent; a 'can see record, not this field' symptom points to FLS, not the record-access layers.

questions.q: In the walkthrough, why couldn't the Tier 1 agent edit the escalated case even though OWD was Public Read Only?
options: Public Read Only already grants edit access, so the problem was elsewhere
The agent's profile lacked Read on Case entirely
Restriction rules blocked all access to the case
The case-team role template granted Tier 2 members Read only, not Edit
questions.explain: OWD gave baseline read access as designed; the actual cause was the case-team role template granting Read instead of Edit to the escalated tier.

questions.q: What is the key difference between troubleshooting and a periodic access review?
options: They are the same activity with different names
Troubleshooting is reactive (triggered by a reported problem); an access review is proactive and scheduled
Access reviews only check field-level security
Troubleshooting only applies to Apex code, not UI access
questions.explain: Troubleshooting responds to a specific reported symptom, while an access review proactively checks for stale or excessive access nobody has reported yet.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say View All and Modify All deserve periodic re-justification rather than a one-time grant?
options: Because they bypass restriction rules entirely and are easy to leave in place long after the original reason is gone
Because they expire automatically after 90 days
Because they are disabled by default in every edition
Because only Apex code can grant them
questions.explain: View All/Modify All override restriction-rule narrowing (Lesson 16) and are exactly the kind of broad, easy-to-forget grant an access review should catch.
